 Vs.

full_judgment:
Nozrul Islam Chowdhury J: This, Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause why the judgment and order dated 20-2-1994 passed by 1st Court of Settlement, Dhaka in Case No. 51 of 1992 relating to House No.3/4 Segun-bagica, Dhaka dismissing the petition for releasing the petitioners property (by majority judgment) should not be declared to have been" passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 2. Heard the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners and Mr Sukumar Biswas the learned Assistant Attorney-General. appearing on behalf of the respondents, perused the petition and the materials placed before us including the impugned judgment wherefrom it transpires that the 1st Court of Settlement was constituted by two other members of them The Chairman delivered the impugned judgment with whom one of the Members i.e. Mr Md Amanullah a member agreed with the Chairman in rejecting the case brought under section 7 of the Ordinance being Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 brought by the petitioner and thereby upheld the inclusion of the property in the Ka list of the abandoned buildings by the respondents, while by the dissenting judgment one of the Member of the Court Mr Muhammad Habibur Raman Bhuiyan allowed the case brought by the petitioner directing exclusion of the case property from the 'Ka' list of the abandoned building with a further direction to restore possession of the case property to the applicant. 

 3. We have gone through the entire judgment in minute details where from it is revealed that the majority views disclosed in the impugned judgment is based on a report available with the records maintained by the government where from the learned Chairman and one of its member held the view that the case property formerly belonged to Khan Bahadur Nazir Uddin Ahmed and on his death his sons and daughters inherited the case property including other building and house left by him. It was also detected in the majority judgment that Mr Kamal Uddin got the case property in his exclusive share upon an. amicable partition amongst his co sharers and Kamal Uddin joined Pakistan Foreign Service and after liberation of Bangladesh he opted for Pakistan and died in Etiophya where he was serving as Ambassador of Pakistan, on the death of Kamaluddin his wife and children also opted for Pakistan, therefore, the government respondents declared the property as abandoned bringing it in the Ka list of the abandoned buildings. The other view in the dissenting judgment we find that the learned Member arrived at a finding that the case property was requisitioned by the government on 11-7-73 and it was de-requisitioned on 21-4-80 and the case property was in the possession of the respondents at the time of its inclusion or enlistment. The order of requisition shows that the respondents acknowledged Mrs Shamsunnessa wife of Iate KB Naziruddin Ahmed as the owner of the case property who neither left the country nor relinquished the citizenship of Bangladesh nor abandoned the property, therefore, the learned Member of the Settlement Court was also of the opinion that the respondents cannot disown its owner Mrs Shamsunnessa and on de-requisition of the property on 21-04-80 it instantly devolved on the original owner from whom the property was requisitioned and never on the government respondents. The learned Member of the Settlement Court in his dissenting judgment has also elaborately mentioned the reasons upon which he had dissented with the majority view passed by the Court of Settlement without going in details about the same. We have also noticed that the government at the time of declaring the property as abandoned included the same in the Ka list as also based its decision on an amicable partition amongst the sharers treating the case property in the exclusive share of Mr Kamaluddin. It may be mentioned in this connection that an amicable partition is a partition as long as it is admitted by the co-sharer but the moment when the co-sharers do not admit the amicable partition such partition cannot have any legal effect. In the instant case we find that the petitioners before us are the admitted co-sharers of Mr Kamal Uddin in the property left behind by Mr KB Naziruddin Ahmed and the petitioners are claiming before us that the property left. behind by KB Naziruddin Ahmed are not partitioned amongst its co-sharers. In such view of the matter, we are of the opinion, that the property of Mr Kamal Uddin one of the sons of KB Naziruddin Ahmed must be ascertained first by the government respondent by away of partition and after a legal partition the property belonged to Kamal Uddin can be treated as abandoned, if the law permits, but before ascertainment of the· exclusive share of Kamal Uddin the declaration of the case property as abandoned as has been done by the government respondents is not accept- able. Therefore, we affirm the opinion disclosed in the judgment by the dissenting judgment delivered by the learned Member Mr Muhammad Habibur Rahman Bhuiyan in Case No. 51 of 1992 ( Ka-82- Segunbagicha, Dhaka) so far as it relates to House No.3/4 Segunbagicha, Dhaka. It may also be noted that after the death of Naziruddin Ahmed ownership devolved upon the heirs of Naziruddin Ahmed and Kamauddin Ahmed is one of those heirs left behind by KB Naziruddin Ahmed. The minority view shall prevail over the majority view delivered by the learned Chairman along with another Member in the said case. 

 4. In the result the rule is made absolute with an observation to the effect that the government, if willing to declare and bring the property of Kamaluddin within the mischief of Ordinance 54 of 1985 as an abandoned property in that case the government is at liberty to bring a partition suit within 6 months from date for the purpose of ascertainment of exclusive share of Kamauddin in House No. 3/4 Segunbagicha, Dhaka and then they are at liberty to proceed in accordance with law, in the meantime both the parties are directed to maintain status quo in respect of possession and position of the property, in the event of failure of the Respondents to bring a partition suit within six months, the minority Judgment shall take immediate effect.
